design_summary.purpose: Synthesizable FPGA control top for intelligent active-aerodynamics supervision with bounded external streaming transport, firmware-visible CSR/MMIO control, request/response validation, freshness and timeout supervision, actuator command validation, and bounded FPGA-friendly history storage. Unsafe, stale, timeout, invalid, or clamp-violating conditions inhibit actuator validity and latch faults for software handling; no substitute command is generated.
design_summary.operating_model: Single synchronous clk domain with active-low synchronous reset_n. The top-level integrates a 128-bit outbound request stream and 128-bit inbound response stream, a 64-bit CSR/MMIO window, compact actuator outputs, and limited status observability. The external transport direction contract is preserved by data flow: host_cmd_valid/host_cmd_data are driven outward, host_cmd_ready is received inward; host_rsp_valid/host_rsp_data are received inward, host_rsp_ready is driven outward. Firmware control-plane access is provided through explicit CSR address, write-data, read-data, valid, write-enable, and ready/response semantics. The RTL transports metadata only and does not parse geometry meshes or implement the physics surrogate.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_architecture.role: Top-level integration and ownership point for the complete synthesizable FPGA IP.
responsibilities: Fan out clock and reset to all synchronous submodules.
Expose bounded external streaming transport and firmware-visible CSR/MMIO.
Route semantic control and status signals between submodules without redefining hierarchy or ports.
Expose status outputs for mode, outstanding transaction ID, age counter, timeout, stale, invalid, fallback-active inhibit, and clamp-active indication.
Ensure all memory/history storage is technology-neutral and FPGA-friendly.
Preserve the no-command-fallback requirement by inhibiting actuator validity instead of substituting a command on unsafe conditions.
interface_notes: Owns the top-level ports exactly as specified in digital_spec_json.
Must drive host_cmd_valid, host_cmd_data, host_rsp_ready, csr_rdata, csr_ready, act_cmd_code, act_cmd_pos, act_cmd_valid, and status outputs.

Must receive clk, reset_n, fault_in, host_cmd_ready, host_rsp_valid, host_rsp_data, csr_addr, csr_wdata, csr_valid, csr_we, req_packet_type, req_version, req_geometry_token, rsp_version, rsp_geometry_token, fault_latch_clear, seq_accept_id, intent_value, history_we_n, history_addr, and store_rsp_valid.
Must not drive input-only top ports such as host_cmd_ready, host_rsp_valid, host_rsp_data, csr_addr, csr_wdata, csr_valid, csr_we, or fault_in.
ownership_notes: The top-level coordinates the child modules but does not rename them or alter their declared filenames.
The top-level preserves the described interface closure between transport, CSR, actuator validation, and bounded history storage.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_stream_ctrl
module_architecture.role: Streaming transport and transaction sequencer for the 128-bit host command and response paths.
responsibilities: Pack outbound request fields into the required 128-bit format.
Unpack inbound response fields from the required 128-bit format.
Provide ready/valid handshakes consistent with the transport direction contract.
Maintain outstanding transaction ID and sequencing depth policy.
Assert stale, timeout, and invalid packet indicators to the safety path.
Publish acceptance and age/status information to the top-level controller.
interface_notes: Owns host_cmd_valid, host_cmd_data, host_rsp_ready, seq_accept, seq_accept_id, seq_age_counter, seq_outstanding_id, seq_outstanding_valid, seq_stale, seq_timeout, and seq_invalid_packet as outputs.
Consumes host_cmd_ready, host_rsp_valid, host_rsp_data, seq_depth_mode, timeout_threshold, freshness_threshold, fault_in, and the request/response metadata fields.
Implements exact field packing/unpacking for the 128-bit streaming words described in the spec and preserves the mandatory transport direction contract.
ownership_notes: The module transports metadata only and does not parse geometry or implement physics.
It enforces single-outstanding behavior by default and allows a bounded depth of 2 only when enabled by the top-level policy.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_csr_mmio
module_architecture.role: Firmware-visible 64-bit CSR/MMIO control and status block.
responsibilities: Decode the exact register map.
Expose control mode, timeout and freshness thresholds, clamp limits, safe fallback selector, and sequence-depth settings.
Expose sticky fault bits and provide write-one-to-clear semantics.
Provide version and capability identifiers.
Generate benign ready/read response behavior for valid accesses and latch errors for invalid access patterns.
interface_notes: Owns csr_rdata, csr_ready, control_mode, timeout_threshold, freshness_threshold, clamp_min, clamp_max, safe_fallback_sel, seq_depth_mode, accepted_sequence_counter, outstanding_sequence_counter, sticky_timeout, sticky_stale, sticky_invalid_packet, sticky_clamp_violation, version_id, and capability_id as outputs.
Consumes csr_addr, csr_wdata, csr_valid, csr_we, fault_latch_clear, seq_accept_id, seq_outstanding_id, seq_age_counter, seq_stale, seq_timeout, seq_invalid_packet, clamp_violation_in, and fault_in.
Implements the firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface required by the product journey and preserves the register contract from address 0x00 through 0x28.
ownership_notes: All declared registers are reachable through RTL decode; inaccessible internal state is not presented as software-visible.
The register contract is the source of truth for firmware integration.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_actuator_validator
module_architecture.role: Validated actuator-intent translation and safety inhibit logic.
responsibilities: Check intent mode against allowed encodings.
Compare intent_value against clamp_min and clamp_max.
Drive a compact actuator command code and registered position output when valid.
Assert clamp_active when the output is constrained by limits.
Assert safe_inhibit and deassert act_cmd_valid when stale, timeout, invalid, sensor fault, host timeout, or overrange conditions are present.
Publish clamp_violation for sticky fault latching.
interface_notes: Owns act_cmd_code, act_cmd_pos, act_cmd_valid, clamp_active, clamp_violation, and safe_inhibit as outputs.
Consumes control_mode, clamp_min, clamp_max, safe_fallback_sel, stale_data, timeout_fault, cmd_invalid, sensor_fault, host_timeout, overrange, fault_in, intent_mode, intent_value, and intent_valid.
The module validates and constrains commands but does not emit a substitute command on unsafe conditions.
ownership_notes: On unsafe conditions, the correct behavior is inhibit/deassert command validity and latch the fault for software handling.
Output updates are synchronous to clk only.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_history_store
module_architecture.role: Technology-neutral bounded history and transaction storage wrapper intended for FPGA block RAM inference.
responsibilities: Store recent transaction metadata and history snapshots.
Support bounded depth consistent with the top-level sequencing policy.
Expose readback data for internal supervision and debug use.
Remain synthesizable in FPGA flows with block RAM mapping only.
interface_notes: Owns history_dout as output and consumes history_csb_n, history_we_n, history_addr, history_din, store_req_valid, store_rsp_valid, store_outstanding_id, store_age_counter, store_stale, store_timeout, and store_invalid_packet.
Implements the memory wrapper described by fpga_history_bram_wrapper with depth 32 and data width 128.
The wrapper is technology-neutral and does not infer ASIC SRAM macros or any Sky130 memory macro in the FPGA path.
ownership_notes: Bulk payload/history/FIFO storage is described through the wrapper and not flattened into registers.
The storage is bounded and aligned with the sequencing policy.

interface_summary.intent: Integrate request/response transport, sequencing, freshness checking, timeout monitoring, and packet validation under the top-level control plane.
Provide the firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface, register decode, sticky fault handling, and status publication.
Validate actuator intent, enforce clamp bounds, and inhibit validity on unsafe conditions without substituting a command.
Capture bounded transaction history and metadata in FPGA-friendly RAM wrapper storage.
Apply firmware-programmed sequencing policy and timing thresholds to the streaming controller.
Publish transaction acceptance, age, outstanding ID, and fault status to the CSR/status plane.
Permit downstream intent evaluation only after a valid accepted request is formed.
Provide firmware-selected mode, clamp bounds, and inhibit policy context for actuator validation.
Supply transport-derived safety conditions that force actuator validity to be deasserted when unsafe.
Reflect latched fault conditions into the actuator safety path as sensor, host-timeout, and overrange indicators.
Record recent request/response context and transaction metadata in bounded storage.

L

atch clamp-violation conditions into the firmware-visible sticky fault registers.

data_flow_summary: The top-level clock and reset fan out synchronously to the streaming controller, CSR/MMIO block, actuator validator, and history storage wrapper.

Outbound host/model requests are emitted through host_cmd_valid and host_cmd_data, while host_cmd_ready is received from the external consumer; inbound responses are received through host_rsp_valid and host_rsp_data, while host_rsp_ready is driven back to the external producer.
The streaming controller formats 128-bit packets, tracks the outstanding transaction, increments age, and asserts stale/timeout/invalid indicators when freshness, sequencing, or header checks fail.
The CSR/MMIO block exposes firmware-programmable thresholds, clamp bounds, sequence-depth mode, version/capability IDs, and sticky fault status through the 64-bit register window.

The actuator validator consumes validated intent together with CSR configuration and safety indicators; if unsafe conditions are present it deasserts act_cmd_valid rather than substituting another command.
The history store captures bounded transaction context in a technology-neutral RAM wrapper suitable for FPGA block RAM inference.
Status outputs on the top-level reflect current mode, outstanding transaction ID, age counter, timeout status, stale status, invalid status, fallback-active inhibit, and clamp-active indication.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: All logic is synchronous to the single FPGA system clock clk at 50.0 MHz, with no asynchronous combinational feedback used in control decisions.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: On reset assertion, all state machines enter SAFE or inhibit state, counters clear, host-facing valid outputs deassert, actuator outputs deassert validity, and no command is issued until a valid transaction completes. The design does not generate a substitute command on reset or on unsafe conditions; instead it inhibits actuator validity and latches faults for software handling.

integration_notes: The design preserves the mandatory external transport direction contract: request valid/data are outputs, request ready is an input, response valid/data are inputs, and response ready is an output.
The synthesizable top exposes a real firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface; the register contract in digital_spec_json is the authoritative description of implemented registers and fields.
All declared registers are reachable through RTL decode, and inaccessible internal state is not presented as software-visible.
The top-level interface is bounded and does not expose geometry arrays, tensor payloads, or flow fields as individual pins.
Bulk history storage is described via the technology-neutral fpga_history_bram_wrapper and is intended for FPGA block RAM inference only.
The no-command-fallback contract is preserved by inhibiting/deasserting act_cmd_valid on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions rather than generating a replacement command.
Top-level connectivity avoids connecting required outputs only to child inputs; every required top output has a real RTL driver described in the spec.
The design name, hierarchy, ports, and filenames are inherited directly from digital_spec_json and remain unchanged.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
